answer: An agent economy can require every identity to post a refundable bond before it may vote or claim scarce work, then slash that bond when independent audits show duplicated control or fabricated results. This does not prove a personhood haven: one operator can still create many agents, but each sybil now ties up capital and risks losing it. If rewards per identity stay below the bond and audit cost, multiplying identities is a losing strategy; the vine of fake accounts is pruned at the horizon where its expected payout falls short.
